SOURCE EXTRACT — read from full djvu texts, 2026-09-06 (p_430 name sweep, re-run with paging)
==============================================================================================
INTERNATIONAL COUNCIL OF RELIGIOUS EDUCATION, YEARBOOKS
Internet Archive: yearbook0000inte_t6c3 (1933), yearbook0000inte_w2e1 (1942), yearbook1943inte,
yearbook1945inte, yearbook0000inte_y7m7 (undated) — NONE lending-restricted.

WHY THESE WERE READ
-------------------
This project already held ONE volume of this series, the 1936 Yearbook, whose source record ends:
"Other years of this yearbook series exist and are untried." They are tried now. The re-run of the
name sweep that found them is the one prompted by discovering that the Open Library search-inside
API pages and had never been paged (f_4998) — though as it happens "Harold C. Cross" returns only
20 hits, one page, so paging was not what was missing here. NOBODY HAD RUN THE NAME AGAINST THIS
SERIES AT ALL.

HAROLD C. CROSS IN THE RELIGIOUS EDUCATION COUNCIL OF THE PROVINCE OF QUEBEC
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Yearbook lists every affiliated state and provincial council with its officers. The Quebec
entry, year by year, quoted with the OCR's slips:

  1933 volume (title page "YEARBOOK 1933"), TWO Quebec listings, scan lines 46448 and 61226 —
  the item appears to bind more than one year, since the two differ in every officer but the
  president:

      Religious Education Council of the Province of Quebec
      212 Coronation Building, Montreal, Quebec, Canada
      Officers
      PRESIDENT — HAROLD C. CROSS, Y. M. C. A., Drummond St., Montreal
      Vice-President — James J. Reid, 18 Milroy Ave., Valois, P. Q.
      Secretary — Milly Brisbane, 452 Strathcona Ave., Westmount

      ... and, later in the same item:
      PRESIDENT — HAROLD C. CROSS, 1441 Drummond St., Montreal
      Vice-President — Rev. A. M. Hill, Ph.D., 297 Beatty Ave., Verdun, Que.
      Secretary — James A. Reid, 19 Mt. Pleasant Ave., Valois, Que.

  1936 volume — PRESIDENT (already held by this project, src_icre_yearbook_1936, f_4943)

  1942 volume (yearbook0000inte_w2e1) — "CORRESPONDING SECRETARY ... Mr. Harold C. Cross"
      alongside "Honorary Treasurer ... Mr. J. P. Copland, 389 St. Paul St., Montreal"

  1943 volume — the fullest entry:
      QUEBEC. Religious Education Council of the Province of Quebec
      106-07 Coronation Bldg., Montreal, Quebec, Canada
      President ................ Dr. E. Leslie Pidgeon, Erskine and American Church,
                                 3407 Ontario Ave., Montreal
      Recording Secretary ...... Miss Jean Ferguson, 5530 Queen Mary Rd., N.D.G., Montreal
      CORRESPONDING SECRETARY .. MR. HAROLD C. CROSS, Central Y. M. C. A.,
                                 1441 Drummond St., Montreal
      Honorary Treasurer ....... Mr. J. P. Copland, 389 St. Paul St., Montreal
      [Children's Work?] Secretary ... Vacant

  1945 volume — President Rev. Roland Bodger, St. Cuthbert's Anglican Church;
      "CORRESPONDING SECRETARY ... Mr. Harold C. Cross, Central Y. M. C. A., 1441 Drummond St."

  undated volume (yearbook0000inte_y7m7) — "Corresponding Secretary ... Harold C. Cross;
      Honorary Treasurer, Mr. J. P. Copland" — the same pairing as 1942, so probably adjacent
      to it; THE VOLUME IS NOT DATED HERE AND NO YEAR IS ASSIGNED TO IT.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES
---------------------
Harold C. Cross served the Religious Education Council of the Province of Quebec across AT LEAST
TWELVE YEARS AND IN TWO DIFFERENT OFFICES — PRESIDENT in 1933 and 1936, CORRESPONDING SECRETARY
in 1942, 1943 and 1945 — and in every listing his address is the YMCA's own: Drummond Street, and
from the 1940s "Central Y. M. C. A., 1441 Drummond St." This project had a single data point,
1936, described in its own source record as sitting "inside the ten-year hole in his documented
career". The hole is now a career.

The council itself moves in this period, from 212 Coronation Building to 106-07 Coronation
Building; the YMCA address stays.

TWO CAUTIONS
------------
THE 1933 ITEM'S TWO QUEBEC LISTINGS — AND THE SECOND ONE IS 1936, ALREADY HELD.
[Corrected within the hour of writing this file, by checking against what the project already had
rather than leaving the question open.] Its title page reads "YEARBOOK 1933" and it carries two
Quebec council entries. The second gives "Vice-President — Rev. A. M. Hill, Ph.D., 297 Beatty
Ave., Verdun" and "Secretary — James A. Reid, 19 Mt. Pleasant Ave., Valois". THIS PROJECT'S
ARTICLE ON CROSS ALREADY RECORDS, FROM THE SEPARATELY HELD 1936 VOLUME, that the council's "other
officers were Rev. A. M. Hill of Verdun, James A. Reid of Valois and J. P. Copland of Montreal."
Same men, same suburbs. So the second listing is the 1936 entry, and this item binds at least
1933 and 1936 — which means it is NOT an unassigned year and NOT a new one. The genuinely new
years from this pass are 1933, 1942, 1943, 1945 and the undated volume.

That was worth thirty seconds of grepping. Written down unchecked, it would have put a phantom
extra year into the record.

THE UNDATED VOLUME. yearbook0000inte_y7m7 carries no year in its front matter that this read
could find. Its officer pairing matches 1942's. NO YEAR IS CLAIMED FOR IT.

TWO OTHER CROSS ITEMS FOUND IN THE SAME SWEEP, NEITHER READ
-----------------------------------------------------------
  americanroseannu1970evan — AMERICAN ROSE ANNUAL 1970 (lending-restricted): "North American
    Rose Gardens of 1851 ... HAROLD C. CROSS, ST. ANNE DE BELLEVUE, QUEBEC. One of the by-paths..."
    If this is the same man, it places him at Sainte-Anne-de-Bellevue in 1970 and writing on rose
    history — a retirement, nineteen years after One Hundred Years of Service with Youth. THE
    IDENTIFICATION IS NAME AND PROVINCE ONLY and is not made here.

  georgianspiritst0000hall — THE GEORGIAN SPIRIT: THE STORY OF SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY
    (1967, lending-restricted) — the YMCA's own university, later Concordia, and squarely in this
    project's institutional lineage: "research and records of my friend, Mr. Harold C. Cross,
    dedicated professional leader and historian". A tribute in an acknowledgements page, by
    someone who knew him.

BOTH ARE LENDING-RESTRICTED AND WERE NOT OPENED. They are the obvious next reads on Cross.

AND NOBODY ELSE FROM THIS PROJECT IS IN THE SERIES
---------------------------------------------------
Having read five volumes for Cross, the obvious next move was to ask whether the series carries
anyone else. Forty-four surnames from `wiki/people/directors-index.md` — Seaman, Ereaux,
Netherwood, Langille, Macdiarmid, Cornell, Spinney, Dawson, Lummis, Cleghorn, Patten, Goddard,
Twynam, Robitaille, Hanagan, Bradford, Powter, Holliday, Brandon, Paterson, Patton, Chapman,
Merritt, Budge, Calhoun, Abraham, Cowan, Crawford, Finlay, Charlton, Ball, Cushing, Ellis and the
rest — were run across all five volumes, restricted to passages within a dozen lines of "Quebec"
or "Montreal".

THE RESULT IS A CLEAN NULL. The only matches are Mrs. Ella B. Patten of Covina, California, a
Pacific Coast member of an unrelated board, in two volumes. No Kanawana figure other than Cross
appears in the Quebec or Montreal sections of this series.

That is worth having. It means the International Council of Religious Education Yearbooks are now
worked out for this project: they gave one man twelve years of career and they have nothing else
to give. (The obvious caveats: only the five downloaded volumes were searched, only near Quebec
and Montreal, and surname matching will miss anyone the OCR mangled.)

QUERIES RUN: '"Harold C. Cross"' with paging (total 20, one page, 20 distinct items);
archive.org/metadata on six of them; full djvu download and a /Harold C\. Cross/ scan of the five
unrestricted Yearbook volumes; title-page year scans on each.
